1.2 Tier 3A: Virtual Advisory for Mercury in Yellow Perch

Virtual advisory values were generated using by modelling the relationship between fish length and contaminant concentration for Yellow Perch and Mercury. For each region, the function fits a log-log linear model (lm(log(Value) ~ log(Length)) to evaluate whether a significant relationship exists (p ≤ 0.05). If so, predicted concentrations are generated across a continuous length range, and then averaged within fixed 5 cm bins. Advisory levels are assigned using MECP-defined contaminant- and population-specific (General/Sensitive) thresholds to the mean predicted concentrations. If no significant relationship is detected, advisory levels are based on the mean concentration of all observations within each bin.

Figure 1.2: Virtual Mercury advisories in Yellow Perch. Predicted concentrations (curve) and observed values (points) by region using power regression model, compared to MECP advisory limits for MERCURY (dashed lines).

1.3 Tier 3B: Comparison of contaminant concentrations in Yellow Perch in AOC to reference

To assess differences in fish contamination between the AOC and reference sites, contaminant–length relationships were modeled using Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), allowing for non-linear associations. For each priority contaminant and indicator species, we first tested whether the shape of the concentration–length relationship differed significantly between AOC and reference fish. Where models supported statistically similar trends (non-significant interaction), we compared size-adjusted contaminant levels using estimated marginal means. Where shapes differed significantly, contaminant concentration values were compared by GAM-predicted values at standardized lengths (e.g., 45cm) commonly consumed for each fish species. A threshold of α = 0.05 was used to evaluate statistical significance throughout.

Figure 1.3: Mercury concentration in Yellow Perch by length in the AOC compared to reference sites.


Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) were used to model the relationship between fish length and mercury concentrations for Yellow Perch in the AOC and reference sites (Lake Ontario, St. Lawrence River). The length-contaminant relationship differed significantly between sites (interaction test p = 1.56e-10). Model-predicted concentrations were compared at a standardized fish length of 20 cm. At this length, the predicted mercury concentration was 0.16 µg/g (95% CI: 0.14–0.18) in the AOC. Predicted concentrations in reference site(s) were: Lake Ontario: 0.08 µg/g (95% CI: 0.07–0.09); St. Lawrence River: 0.12 µg/g (95% CI: 0.1–0.13).

1.4 Tier 3C: Temporal Trends

Temporal trends in Yellow Perch for Mercury were analyzed across all years using Generalized Additive Models (GAMs). The analysis was limited to the three most sampled length bins for the species, and results are presented separately by region. These plots help assess whether contaminant concentrations are declining, stable, or increasing over time within each region.
